questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**misanthorpe**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The incorrectly spelt word if corrected results in the formation of '**misanthrope**'.
 
• Let us understand the meaning of the correctly formed words:
 
• Misanthrope: It means a person who hates or avoids other people.
 
 
• Example: *The haughty rich man was such a misanthrope who had spiked wire all around his yard to intimidate his neighbors away.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the only incorrectly spelt word is: *Misanthorpe*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Mascot: a person, animal, or thing that is thought to bring good luck.
 
• Socialite: a person who often goes to fashionable parties and social events and gets written about in newspapers, magazines, etc.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Does the manufacturer have a website where details __of the product are available__?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**No substitution required**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined segment does not need to be substituted.
 
• The aforementioned line poses a general query, and as is well known, that the preposition "**of**" denotes **associations** between other words, such as **belonging**, things made of different things, items that contain other things, or a point of comparison.
 
 
• Example: *The lady in the main office is the CEO of this company.*
 
 
 
• That is why the use of** **the** preposition** "of" is **appropriately** applied in the sentence.
 
• Additionally, the statement is discussing the specifics of a particular product, and the helping verb "**are**" is used as a **simple present** assisting **verb** for the **noun** "**details**" in the sentence.
 
• Consequently, the use of "are" is grammatically and conceptually **correct**.
 
• Therefore, the appropriate response is: *No substitute is required*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Lets understand the implication of the remaining **prepositions:**

 
• **For**: When discussing a rationale or **purpose** for anything, we use the preposition "for."

 
 
• Example: *I am going for a walk with Sofia.*
 
 
 
• **On**: When referring to a place on a** surface**, we use the preposition "on."
 
 
• Example: *I am putting the watch on the dressing table.*

questions.question:

Hopefully, I __will have got__ my driving license by the end of this year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **No improvement required. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

• **Example:** *By night, I will have finished my homework.*
 
 
 
• *​*The given sentence is grammatically correct.

• The tenses only serve to convey the passage of time.
 
• **The "Future Perfect Tense" is used to represent an action that is anticipated to be finished before a specific future time.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• **"On the way"** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct usage is **"In the way" **instead of** "On the way."**
 
• The phrase "in the way" refers to the type of thing being described, thought of, etc.
 
• **We use "on the way" when we talk about the route, direction, or path to somewhere.**
 
• **In the given sentence, we talk about the people's appearance and their personality traits, not about the route or direction.**
 
 
• **Examples:** *There is a very big difference in the way she looked at you today. Her eyes were filled with hatred. *
 
• *We will have our breakfast on the way to Manali. *
 
 

*​*The correct sentence is: **People vary greatly in the way they appear and in their personality traits.**
